fields.statement: QA with a fresh build of cs/leaf-contract (go build -trimpath to $TMPDIR, scratch repo and root): rhiza add capability with files and must_not, rhiza set failure_waiver and rhiza apply with files/must_not all wrote and rhiza show read them back; rhiza add constraint with files refused exit 2 (known fields acceptance, statement); a capability field file refused exit 2 listing failure_waiver, files, must_not. A fake-agent run wrote brief.md listing Files:, Must not: and Failure waiver: under each leaf acceptance for the fields it has and none for a leaf without them.

QA with the built binary on a hold-workflow plan run: review-check failed exit 1 naming cap-b lacks files, must_not, a failure case; a parent with a live child was skipped and an uppercase FAILURE CASE passed; a waiver satisfied the failure case; whitespace-only must_not reported as lacking; round 2 printed both the leaf-contract and confirmed-finding failures; round 3 still failed with no question or asked entry; once fixed, round 4 passed leaving the confirmed finding as a question; retiring the child made the parent a leaf and review-check failed naming it.

QA with the built binary: rhiza run findings accepted kind no-failure-case, refused no-failure exit 2 listing eight kinds ending oversized-leaf, no-failure-case; a confirmed no-failure-case finding failed review-check at round 2 and became a question at round 4; rhiza guide check-qa severities block names no-failure-case major.

QA with the built binary: rhiza guide plan-reviewer lists eight kinds with no-failure-case after oversized-leaf, narrows missing-acceptance to vague, unrunnable or full-suite, and says never to record what rhiza run review-check checks or rhiza check reports; plan-reviser and plan-critic name no-failure-case; no topic says seven kinds.

QA with the built binary: rhiza guide plan-recipes Leaves section teaches files, must_not, failure_waiver, the words failure case and one fresh session, its apply recipe carrying files= and must_not=; rhiza guide planner names files, must_not and the failure case.
